summary: Grant County, OR site: an L-4 tower from 1934 or 1938 replaced by a 30-ft R-6 tower in 1962-63, moved to Antelope Mountain in 1974, where it still stands.

facts.design: 30' treated timber tower with R-6 flat cab (1962-63); earlier 33' pole tower with L-4 cab (1938)
facts.status_note: The tower was moved to Antelope Mountain in 1974 and stands there; no source read describes what remains at the Lake Butte site

access.note: No source read describes access to the Lake Butte site now, or whether Antelope Mountain is open to visitors

events.note: 20-foot native timber tower with L-4 cab per Forest Lookouts; firelookout.com says the site was established in the early 1930s
33-foot pole or round timber tower with L-4 cab
Coast and Geodetic Survey station description calls the tower about 40 feet high
Grub Creek fire reported from the station, July 13, 1961
New 30-foot treated timber R-6 flat tower completed late in 1962 per a 1962 annual report; the register and firelookout.com say 1963
Shots fired through the lookout post while the lookout was away from the tower; reported by the Blue Mountain Eagle
Tower moved to Antelope Mountain; the register says only 'the 1970s'
Registered June 23, 2011; nominated by Ray Kresek

corrections.why: 6.1 m is 20 feet, the height Forest Lookouts gives for the 1934 timber tower. The tower in place from 1962-63 until 1974, the one moved to Antelope Mountain, is 30 feet (about 9.1 m) per the register and firelookout.com.

corrections.proposed: 30' treated timber tower with R-6 flat cab (1962-63)
corrections.why: L-4 was the cab on the earlier 33-foot pole tower (1938). The tower from 1962-63 that was moved in 1974 had an R-6 flat cab.
The tower was moved to Antelope Mountain in 1974, and firelookout.com describes it there as the present tower. It is not gone; it is at another site.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts gives a 20-foot tower in 1934; firelookout.com says the site was established in the early 1930s; the register dates its 33-foot L-4 tower to 1938. The story gives the 1934 and 1938 dates from Forest Lookouts and the register and notes firelookout.com's version.
Forest Lookouts quotes a 1962 annual report saying the tower was completed late in 1962. The register and firelookout.com give 1963. The story uses 1962 and notes the 1963 dates.

The register and firelookout.com give 30 feet for the R-6 tower; Forest Lookouts gives 33 feet for the 1938 tower; a 1946 Coast and Geodetic Survey description says about 40 feet. The story gives the 1946 figure and notes it differs.
Forest Lookouts and firelookout.com give 1974; the register says the 1970s. The story gives 1974 and notes the register's wording.
firelookout.com says 12 miles north of John Day; the 1946 survey description, quoted by Forest Lookouts, says about 11 miles north of John Day. Minor; the story uses firelookout.com's figure.

notes_for_editor: The brief's height_m (6.1 m) and design (L-4) describe the 1934 or 1938 tower, not the 30-foot R-6 tower that was moved in 1974, so both are corrected. The brief's status 'gone' is corrected to 'relocated' because the tower stands on Antelope Mountain. Antelope Mountain's own history (a first tower in 1930, a different site) is not part of Lake Butte's record and is not used. The 1974 move bid described on the Antelope Mountain pages of Forest Lookouts and another site was seen only in search snippets and is not used. No source read describes what, if anything, remains at the Lake Butte site today. The staffing entry is from the 1964 report, which implies a lookout was on duty; no staffing history after 1964 was found.
